initial_prompts.name: tall
initial_prompts.label: 길쭉형
initial_prompts.direction: Very TALL, thin, awkwardly charming bean-shaped body in a frontal seated pose, tiny rounded head at the top, very long loose floppy ears, tiny dot eyes spaced unevenly, long narrow front legs drawn as two simple U shapes, short tiny paws, a curved little tail wrapping alongside. Like the tall simple doodle dogs in style references 3 and 4. Head only about one quarter of full character height, torso and legs deliberately stretched. Slight imperfect left/right balance. Gray floppy ears and gray upper sides/back with large white chest/face central stripe.
initial_prompts.prompt:
Create one ORIGINAL full-body hand-drawn DOODLE DOG concept, using images 1-4 as STYLE AND DEFORMATION / PROPORTION references and image 5 ONLY to identify the individual's coat/ears. The drawings in references have loose thin black ink contours, innocent dot eyes, a solid oval black nose, very few strokes, funny deliberately irregular proportions, and simple flat shapes. Use this hand-drawn vocabulary rather than photographic anatomy. Do not copy a particular dog from the reference sheets or include their watermarks, logos, wording or sheet layout. No pixel art, grid, square stepped edges, low-resolution rendering or 48px limitations. Smooth high-resolution curves, slightly wobbly hand-drawn line, playful imperfection, no scribble mess or detailed fur hatching, no realistic rendering, gradients or 3D effects. One clean original character on a plain white background with generous whitespace, no props, labels, caption, collar, tongue or scene. Preserve the SAME real pet's few identifiers: drooping rounded gray ears, gray upper head and back, broad WHITE blaze down center forehead into white muzzle, white chest and white feet, little dark nose and dot eyes. Render gray marks as sparse FLAT light-to-medium gray fill with thin dark outline; all remaining areas white. Muzzle fluffy indicated by just 2-3 loose bumps, not fur strands. Full-body, quiet friendly expression, head looking toward viewer, whole dog visible. Deformation is the MAIN creative change below:

initial_prompts.name: pudgy
initial_prompts.label: 통통형
initial_prompts.direction: Very SHORT and PUDGY squashy doodle dog, big broad floppy-eared head nearly half total height, small rounded loaf/bag-shaped body and extremely short bean paws, loosely sitting with tiny forepaws spread apart, mild tilt to head and uneven ears, placid cute expression. Minimal thin wobbly contour like the squat cartoon dogs in reference 2. This is rounded flat line-doodle, not detailed plush illustration or glossy chibi. Sparse gray ear and back shapes, broad white forehead/muzzle and chest.

initial_prompts.name: wonky
initial_prompts.label: 비대칭형
initial_prompts.direction: A quirky ASYMMETRIC doodle dog standing sideways with its head turned toward viewer. Unusually long wavy horizontal peanut-shaped torso, small off-center oval head with one ear drawn lower, thin crooked stick-like legs of slightly irregular lengths ending on one ground level, little bent tail, amusing lopsided silhouette. Use a handful of simple freehand curves and dot eyes, thin black line, flat sparse gray patches. Refer to the stretched funny side-view dogs of reference 3 and irregular full-body drawings of reference 2; this must feel like a friendly casual notebook sketch, not realistic adult anatomy. Keep the white middle face/muzzle, gray floppy ears/back and white little feet.

final_prompts.name: tall
final_prompts.label: 길쭉형
final_prompts.shape: Front-facing sitting dog with an absurdly TALL skinny sack-shaped body, little oval head only one fifth of total height, long droopy ears, two long U-shaped front legs. Slightly uneven dot eyes. Comically elongated torso, very little anatomy.
final_prompts.prompt: Make ONE original naive DOODLE drawing. The attached sheets are the PRIMARY references for BOTH the simple sparse line quality AND the exaggerated body proportions. Aim especially at the very simple skinny odd dogs in the first attached sheet and the tall front-facing dogs in the second. It should look casually drawn by hand in a notebook in 15 seconds, NOT a finished pet illustration, plush character, painted portrait, manga or polished vector mascot. MAIN SHAPE: Front-facing sitting dog with an absurdly TALL skinny sack-shaped body, little oval head only one fifth of total height, long droopy ears, two long U-shaped front legs. Slightly uneven dot eyes. Comically elongated torso, very little anatomy. Thin black pen lines, gently wobbly/uneven contours, a few small loose overlaps or imperfect connections, two tiny solid DOT eyes and one tiny black OVAL nose, one simple mouth curve. No detailed fur, toes, eyelashes, shiny highlights, shadows, crosshatching, texture or internal anatomy. Maximal simplicity, large blank white areas. Mostly black line on plain WHITE with ONLY a sparse flat gray area on drooping ears and upper back; leave broad white stripe down forehead and white muzzle/chest/paws to represent the same gray-and-white pet. No colored rendering, gradients, watercolor, mottled coats or thick furry outlines. One complete full-body dog centered with generous whitespace, no caption, text, logos, watermark, accessories, props or decorative marks. Do not reproduce a reference-sheet dog exactly: invent the form described above. Use smooth high-resolution ink curves, no pixel grid or low-resolution constraints. Express the deformation through the whole head/body/leg silhouette, not just a change of surface style.
